requirements.reason: GPIO, reload, and UART logs are actually updated through host-effect code paths.
168 MHz, reload divided by 1000, and tick increments are explicit.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The target path fully specifies PB6/7, default 9600, 8N1, RXNE, and NVIC 0/0.
Push-pull/pull-up/25 MHz settings are present; direction drives outputs directly and ignores speed.
Host LED states for PD12-15 are stored and updated by index. D:35-36 permits observable arrays as hardware-effect equivalents; absence of physical BSRRL/BSRRH registers alone is not a defect.
Bit 0 is active-high and initially cleared; the low-level branch releases the button.
The prescribed TM LIS3DSH initialization receives 2G/50Hz. D:39 fixes the SPI1/TM device boundary and permits low-level configuration stubs.

12-bit, continuous, Prescaler8, and 144-cycle parameters are explicitly passed to initialization. Host structures/configuration stubs need not access a physical ADC. This judgment does not claim verification of target SPL compilation or hardware configuration.
The target uses AHB2 RNG and reads DRDY; host ready/value provide the corresponding observable inputs.
The nine startup stages are in the correct order.
The exact CRLF-terminated text is sent after USART initialization.
The clock is updated before calling SysTick_Config with clock/1000.
A nonzero target configuration result loops forever and prevents subsequent startup. The host SysTick model's fixed success does not constitute testing the failure path.
The target enables GPIOA and configures PA0 input; the host clears bit 0 and debounce state.
The direction enumeration values 0, 1, and 2 are correct.
The left-side 10/01/00/default-00 mapping is complete.
The right-side 10/01/00/default-00 mapping is complete.
speed is retained and discarded; there is no PWM.
Both sides forward produce 1010.
Both sides reverse produce 0101.
Left stopped and right forward produce 0010.
Left forward and right stopped produce 1000.
Left stopped and right reverse produce 0001.
Left reverse and right stopped produce 0100.
Left forward and right reverse produce 1001.
Left reverse and right forward produce 0110.
STOP on both sides clears all four outputs.
Clock/mode and host initial states are complete; the target explicitly clears the four bits through BSRRH.
Direction combinations avoid 11; bits that must be low are cleared before high bits are set. This does not establish that physical transient tests passed.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The nine IDs match the nine functions in order.
Valid IDs 0-8 immediately invoke the lookup-table entry, without framing or ACK.
Validity is checked before writing callme; empty queues are not dispatched, and invalid negative values do not alter state.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Indices 0-3 read the corresponding bits; out-of-range indices return -1.
Every tick increments the clock; continuous high counting must reach 250 to become pressed.
A low level immediately clears the count and sets the released state.
Only change tracking, switch/break, and laststate updates occur.
The roll formula atan2f(y,z)*180/pi is correct.
The pitch formula atan2f(-x,sqrt(y squared+z squared))*180/pi is correct.
GPIOD and push-pull outputs are enabled; BSRRH is written and host initial outputs are cleared.
A valid index sets GPIOD_output[12+i] to 1, which is the required host equivalent of setting the LED. A physical BSRRL write is not required on the host.
A valid index clears GPIOD_output[12+i], preserving observable LED-off semantics. Absence of a physical BSRRH write is not a missing host-model behavior.
Only indices 0-3 are accepted; invalid values do not write GPIO.
History time is updated only when strictly >1000; UART is still checked each step.
The prescribed TM function is called with 2G/50Hz and the host returns 0. Target configuration details are not presented as proof of hardware execution.
Stored three-axis values use the shared read path with floating-point division by 1000.
Clock, independent mode, division, alignment, internal temperature channel, 144 cycles, and enabling are encoded. Empty host configuration stubs are allowed without actual register side effects.

The source expresses start -> wait -> read, but the host start function is empty and ADC_GetFlagStatus always returns SET, making not-ready unrepresentable. D:11-12 permits configuration stubs, not a data-readiness check fixed to success.
raw is first converted to float; formula parameters and operation order are correct.
The target enables the AHB2 clock before RNG.
The target's no-timeout wait is correct. The host exits after a bounded wait, but returns the old value even if readiness never occurs, without a distinguishable not-ready outcome.
The entire 32-bit value is returned without filtering zero or all ones.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The first NULL slot stores interval*1000 and clears both counter fields.
After traversing full slots, the code ends silently without writes.
Due nonempty tasks execute in slot order and update last_called and numcalls; multiple tasks may run on one tick.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Nonempty tasks print the correct slot number and count.
Execution is sequential and nonpreemptive; NULL slots are skipped, and no removal or priority API exists.
baud=0 emits a warning and selects 9600.
Target calls specify GPIOB alternate function/push-pull/pull-up/100 MHz, USART 8N1, bidirectional operation without flow control, and interrupt priority.
msg is initialized to 200 bytes and USART is enabled.
RXNE reads DR into the queue, dropping the byte if full; other interrupts have no branch action.
The target waits for 0x40 before each character and retains the unbounded wait.
The ring-buffer read is delegated; empty returns 0.
Conversion to signed char precedes return, preserving the convention that FF is -1.
Delegation returns the counter difference.
All five required fields are present.
An enabled buffer reports an error and is skipped; calloc zeros memory and all fields are initialized.
Nonfull buffers write modulo size and increment n_w; full buffers return 0 without overwriting.
Nonempty buffers read modulo size and increment n_r; empty buffers return 0.
Normal objects use n_r==n_w to test emptiness.
A normal nonempty buffer is full when its indices are equal modulo size; invalid objects are separately rejected safely.
Returns n_w-n_r.
A temporary realloc pointer protects the old allocation; success updates size.
Contents are cleared and freed, all fields reset, and the buffer disabled; NULL returns false.
Only contents are memset; counters and configuration are unchanged.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
uint32_t addition by 1 implements modulo-2^32 wraparound.

func1 passes the same argument to func2 and returns its result. D:72 explicitly allows an equivalent host C implementation; downgrading it for not delivering ARM LR instructions exceeds this task's scope.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Required values are public; START/STOP constants do not become a firmware framing protocol.
Pin-indexed arrays are actually updated with only 0 or 1.
The mask modifies only GPIOA_IDR bit 0.
Injected three-axis data is read through the same path.
Injected raw data enters the formula through the same conversion-value entry.
ready/value are stored and no permanent deadlock occurs, but not-ready eventually returns the old value just like ready, without a distinguishable status outcome.
Setting DR and RXNE invokes the same ISR; the host clears the injected state after returning.
Characters are appended to the log with maintained length and bounded capacity.
A single step handles timing/UART/button/tasks without defining main or self-tests.

Generic CircArray objects can be deleted, but UART's internally allocated static msg is not exposed. The complete delivered code has no reachable call freeing it. R:299 requires all allocations to be releasable; this gap is unrelated to permitted configuration stubs.
Null pointers, out-of-range indices, and full buffers have safe branches; the executor does not call NULL tasks.
No UART framing/removal/PWM extensions are added; speed remains ignored.

metric: coverage of 88 statically reviewable requirement leaves; 7 preclassified leaves unassessed
note: All 931 C-source lines and the 107-line header were read, tracing target conditional branches and host adapters separately. Configuration stubs and not-ready semantics were not credited based on function names.
scope_review_policy: R+D host-equivalent task contract; supplied A constrains shared-API methods; configuration stubs allowed, missing required values/paths not invented; Direct not penalized by unsupplied A; no candidate changes
scope_review_notes: R:1–16 and D:7–12 define project-level host-equivalent scope, not reconstruction of real upstream firmware.
D:11–12/A:273–276 allow configuration stubs; this does not waive R-specified configuration values/order.
D:72 allows transparent C semantics for host assembly functionality.
R:299 allocation-release obligation remains applicable regardless of hardware stub permissions.
Original standalone serializers record preliminary decisions; active JSON after this scope reconciliation is authoritative.
